title: C24103860012
paper_title: 数据驱动下磁性元件的磁芯损耗建模

route: decision tree and random forest feature importance
six-model vote using full and selected features
strengths: combines shape-domain reasoning with classification instead of using an opaque classifier alone
reports accuracy/recall/precision/F1 and recognizes perfect classification can be suspicious
identifies very simple waveform descriptors such as kurtosis and high-ranked FFT amplitudes that may support interpretable baselines
risks: the paper describes five-fold cross-validation but also reports separate train/cross-validation/test metrics without a reproducible split contract in the printed appendix
perfect or near-perfect row-level classification does not prove robustness across unseen material/frequency/amplitude regimes
Spearman correlation prose contains likely transcription errors such as s5-s4 coefficient 0.1 described as extremely strong and s4-kurtosis 907 without a decimal
feature-importance values are used as evidence of importance but no grouped stress test checks whether the selected features remain stable across operating conditions

route: six temperature-correction equations with temperature main/interactions
5-fold shuffled KFold in printed linear-regression code
model selection by MSE and R2
strengths: printed appendix actually contains KFold evaluation rather than only a full-data fit
compares multiple explicit temperature hypotheses and keeps the Steinmetz structure interpretable
reports both log-domain and exponentiated-domain error in code, which is important because inverse-log magnifies errors
risks: random shuffled KFold mixes all four temperatures and therefore does not test extrapolation/generalization to an unseen temperature condition
model selection still relies on the same operating-condition support used for calibration; leave-temperature-out or leave-region-out evidence is absent
the conclusion that the added triple interaction is harmful because fit worsens is model/data-specific and does not prove the physical interaction is absent
cross-validation is visible only for one printed material file while tables summarize all four materials, so the full per-material evaluation pipeline is not fully reproducible from the appendix

route: one-way ANOVA/Welch ANOVA with effect size
heatmap and frequency-stratified interpretation of low-loss condition
strengths: unlike S009, explicitly reports effect sizes such as partial eta-squared/Cohen f instead of treating p-values alone as impact magnitude
recognizes in its own discussion that frequency sampling changes the inferred optimal temperature
does not overstate the two nonsignificant pairwise interactions as significant synergy
risks: sorting by frequency and then randomly drawing 50 rows does not guarantee matched frequency distributions and does not control Bm, so operating-condition confounding remains
calling nonsignificant temperature-material/material-waveform interactions independent is stronger than the statistical evidence supports
the recommended 70C/90C optimum changes with frequency, demonstrating that a single raw group mean is not a stable global optimum
sampling randomness itself can alter the conclusion; adjusted regression/ANCOVA with log f/log Bm would use all data and provide clearer conditional effects

route: add IGSE prior as stacked feature
strengths: compares a physics baseline against multiple ML families
explicitly checks error in the original physical scale after log-target modeling
uses a physics-derived IGSE output as a candidate prior feature, a sensible physics-plus-ML pattern in principle
risks: random row-level 8:2 split is labeled generalization evidence although unseen material/temperature/waveform/operating-region validation is not shown
paper says log transform unifies dimensions; log scaling changes numerical scale but does not eliminate physical units/dimensional semantics
printed CatBoost code appends raw maxB rather than log(maxB), despite the text saying frequency and Bm are log transformed; this is a paper-code feature-transform mismatch
printed Q4 code computes kurtosis/skewness but never appends them, and contains no visible IGSE feature or stacking path, so the claimed best CatBoost+IGSE pipeline is not reproduced by the appendix
the variable true_mse accumulates squared errors but is printed as True Mean Squared Error without dividing by sample count

route: two objectives: minimize predicted loss and maximize f*Bm
strengths: the paper at least evaluates multiple optimizer families and later recognizes that other category combinations can outperform the initially narrowed search
bounds for frequency/Bm are visible in the printed PSO fragment, which supports feasibility auditing
risks: 1:1 raw weighted sum predicted_loss - transmission_energy is not equal preference because the objectives have different units and scales; normalization or Pareto treatment is required
EMI is defined as loss/(loss+energy), so smaller is better; calling it an efficiency-maximization indicator is semantically inverted unless reported as a loss fraction
printed appendix contains only PSO code, not the claimed best GWO or GA implementation, so the optimizer ranking is not reproducible from visible code
Q5 retrains a five-basic-feature CatBoost rather than the paper-selected CatBoost+IGSE best Q4 pipeline
exact helper smoke shows the objective converts integer waveform/material ids to Chinese strings and then calls one-hot helpers that compare to integers, collapsing every category vector to all zeros

printed PSO fixes t=25, waveform=3 and material=1 inside the function; the paper tables for T=70/90 and all 48 category combinations therefore require manual code changes or another missing loop/implementation
fixing waveform/material based on Q3 before global multiobjective optimization can remove feasible Pareto-optimal regions, especially because Q3 itself is frequency/Bm-confounded

verified_text_evidence.claim: Q1 feature engineering, DT/RF/logistic results, perfect metrics and six-model vote
Q2 six corrections plus shuffled five-fold KFold printed implementation
Q3 ANOVA/effect sizes, nonsignificant interactions and frequency-sensitive 70C/90C optimum
Q4 nine-model comparison and printed CatBoost path lacking visible IGSE stacking/feature-transform consistency
Q5 weighted scalarization, GA/PSO/GWO claims and printed PSO/category encoding implementation

transfer_lessons: Cross-validation must hold out the unit of generalization being claimed; random KFold across temperatures is not leave-temperature-out evidence.
A nonsignificant interaction is insufficient to assert physical/statistical independence; report uncertainty and power/effect-size bounds.
Feature transforms are part of the schema contract: log/raw/normalized versions must match between prose, train and inference code.
The exact best model named in the paper must have an executable end-to-end path; evaluating a simpler ablation does not validate the claimed final model.
Weighted multiobjective scalarization requires dimensionless normalized objectives or a declared utility function; equal numeric weights do not imply equal preference.
Categorical encoders must have a type/domain contract and unit tests, especially when optimization code maps ids to labels and back.
For multiobjective mixed-variable optimization, do not prune discrete variables from a preliminary unadjusted factor analysis before checking the full feasible Pareto set.
